To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we predict and study the topologically induced Purcell factor enhancement in a polaritonic metamaterial formed by nanowires, and that we show that the topological transition is accompanied by a specific isofrequency shape.
we reveal and study the transition between elliptic and hyperbolic regimes of a metamaterial formed of parallel nanowires and that the extraordinary Purcell factor can be obtained at this transition.

we predict the existence of a topological transition in the dispersion relation of a metamaterial composed of nanowires of a polaritonic material, which implies a specific isofrequency contour, that this metamaterial is characterized by a high Purcell factor in the epsilon-indefinite regime, and that the Purcell factor can be enhanced in spite of the optical losses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of metamaterials for nanophotonic applications.
the design of a metamaterial with a topological transition in the nanowire medium.
the topological properties of metamaterials formed by nanowires of plasmonic material.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the topological transition of the dispersion of a nanowire metamaterial leads to a very specific isosurface, and this implies an extraordinary Purcel factor in spite of the presence of optical losses.
the Purcell factor is not a universal figure of merit for nanowire metamaterials.
a metamaterial composed by parallel polaritonic nanowires exhibits a topological transition that leads to a Purcell factor enhancement, even in the presence of significant optical losses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a new type of topological transition, which is of great importance to the design of metamaterials and metasurfaces.
a topological transition in metamaterials is not only a matter of fundamental interest but also has a radiative implication.
we show how to exploit topological transition in metamaterials to achieve a strong enhancement of light-matter coupling.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the topological transition of epsilon is a key element to enhance the Purcell factor in a medium formed by parallel nanorods of a polaritonic material, and that this enhancement is not related to the hyperbolicity of the medium.
the Purcell factor can be enhanced in the epsilon-indefinite regime by a factor of 10^4, while the losses are not increased.
the Purcell factor is not necessarily enhanced when the nanowires are in the epsilon-negative regime.
